title: 66 or 66.0? Measurement Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Aarav measures his bicycle wheel twice: 66 cm on one tape, 66.0 cm on a finer one. Same wheel, so why does the second reading tell us more? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) we learn to read a measurement digit by digit.

You will see why every measurement needs a unit, the seven SI base units (metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela), and prefixes from nano to kilo. On the bench the decimal point hops step by step to write 0.00016 as 1.6 x 10^-4 and 232.508 as 2.32508 x 10^2, with a live hop counter. Then the four rules for significant figures, a worked example in dimensional analysis (2 L of milk is 2 x 10^-3 m3), precision versus accuracy on a number line, the exam trap about zeros, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 5 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Two readings, one wheel
0:30 Number plus unit: SI base units
1:02 Prefixes, powers of ten
1:13 Scientific notation: the hopping point
1:57 Pause and think: positive or negative power?
2:14 Significant figures: four rules
3:04 Worked example: dimensional analysis
3:43 Precision vs accuracy
4:14 Exam trap: counting zeros
4:39 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Laws of Chemical Combination. When a candle burns away, where does its mass go?
